claim: `run` reads `head` before `keep_alive`, which commits and pushes a `saved` event when the ticket's last event is at least `save_minutes` old; after the reviewer, `git reset --hard head` moves the branch back behind that pushed commit. The review run is then committed on the old head and its push is refused as a non-fast-forward, so the run never reaches the remote and every later push of the branch is refused too (sequence: a ticket in `reviewing`, `rail advance` more than ten minutes after its last event, such as a session coming back from a pause or after an invalid-output review).
check: A test that runs `rail advance` on a ticket in `reviewing` whose last event is older than `[claim] save_minutes`, and asserts that the local branch and the remote branch have the same tip afterwards.

claim: With this engine ticket 8 is no longer `merged`: its contract pull request #11 was merged with no ship, so it becomes `new` with owner `agent` (CONTRACT_MERGED). After ticket 9 merges, the next `rail next` records the merge as the owner's approval of ticket 8 and hands an agent the same contract ticket 9 just delivered; nothing in the change drops ticket 8 or says a person must.
check: After the change, `rail status --json` lists no ticket with owner `agent` whose Done Contract equals that of a merged ticket; here, ticket 8 is dropped before or with the merge.

reason: The sign of life is now written before the review run reads the head it resets the worktree to (review.py); a test with save_minutes = 0 checks the branch stays in step with the remote across two reviews.

Ticket 8 is dropped: a dropped event on its branch and a 'rail drop 8' mark on the counter branch rail/ids. The engine now marks every drop there, so a dropped ticket whose contract reached the base stays dropped when its branch is deleted (state.py, project.py), with a test.

claim: A `cd` the guard can't follow is recognised only when `cd`, `pushd` or `popd` is the first word of a simple command. After `cd OTHER_REPO &&`, a `cd -` inside a brace group, after `then`, or after `!` is missed, so the push to `main` or `gh pr merge` that follows is judged as the other repository's and allowed. This is the sweep's F1 case in another spelling, and `docs/guards.md` says whatever can't be followed is judged as this project's.
check: A guard test that expects deny for `cd OTHER && { cd -; git push origin main; }`, `cd OTHER && if true; then cd -; fi && git push origin main` and `cd OTHER && ! cd - && git push origin main`, where OTHER is another git repository.

claim: The ticket's Why says work a session abandoned is resumed after an hour, but the engine copied in resumes it after `[claim] stale_minutes` = 30 (config.py default, and the ticket's own Look at says 30 minutes). The Why becomes the pull request's description, so the owner is told twice the real limit.

reason: The guard now strips shell keywords ({, !, if, then, elif, else, do, while, until) before reading a command, so a cd or a push behind one is seen; tests cover the four spellings reported and plain keyword commands that must still pass.
The ticket's Why now says 30 minutes with no sign of life, as the engine does.

claim: `_save_note` reads the cache with key `session or ""`, so with no `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` it opens the directory `rail/cache/hooks/` and `rail next` dies with a traceback. Sequence: any Claude session has started in the clone (the SessionStart hook creates that folder), then `rail next --ticket 1` or a bare `rail next` runs from a plain terminal or another agent; the claim is committed before the crash.
check: A test that runs the session-start hook with a session id, then `rail next --ticket NN` with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID unset, and expects exit 0 with an IMPLEMENT brief.

claim: The save hooks don't know a review is running: when the session's PostToolUse hook fires while its own `rail advance` is inside a review (a parallel tool call, or advance run in the background), `save_work` commits and pushes the reviewer's in-scope scratch files. The review's `git reset --hard head` then moves the branch back behind that push, so the `review` commit never reaches the remote and local and remote stay diverged (the same end state as F1).
check: A test whose review command writes a file inside scope_paths and sleeps, runs `rail hook pulse` for the same session meanwhile, and asserts the remote branch has no scratch file and equals the local branch after advance.

reason: cache_read returns nothing for an empty key or a folder, and the save note is only read when the session has an id. Test: test_next_works_from_a_plain_terminal_after_a_claude_session in the framework's tests/test_save.py (framework commit 9104f6c).

An engine command that works in a ticket's worktree (advance, a transition from next, sweep) now holds a per-ticket file lock, and a save skips a ticket that is held. Test: test_a_save_stays_out_while_advance_is_inside_a_review (framework commit 9104f6c); it fails without the hold.

reason: The guard no longer expands variables from the hook's environment: it follows only ~, $HOME and $PWD (the place it followed the command to); any other variable, $OLDPWD included, is judged as this project's. So after `cd OTHER_REPO &&`, `builtin cd - && git push origin main` (or `eval cd - && ...`, or `gh pr merge 5` in place of the push) is still judged as the other repository's and allowed, although the shell is back in this project; this is F3's case in one more spelling.
check: A guard test that `cd OTHER && builtin cd - && git push origin main` and the same with `eval cd -` are denied, next to the existing keyword-spelling tests.

reason: The guard now reads the command that runs: builtin and other wrappers with their own options and arguments are unwrapped (builtin cd -, timeout 60 git push -f, xargs, sudo -u NAME, /usr/bin/git), and the commands of bash -c and eval are judged too. claim: `save_work` passes every dirty path to `git add -A -- <paths>`, which dies with `pathspec did not match any files` for a staged deletion. After `git rm src/old.py` in a ticket's worktree (or one save after `git mv`, which commits only the new name and leaves `D old` staged), every `rail save` exits 2 and the Stop and pulse hooks fail without telling the agent: nothing is pushed and no `saved` event is written, so the work isn't saved and the ticket looks abandoned to other sessions after 30 minutes.
check: A test in tests/test_save.py: claim a ticket, `git rm` (and separately `git mv`) an in-scope file in its worktree, run `rail save` twice, and assert exit 0, a `saved` event, and the deletion on the remote branch.

reason: A save now stages only paths that are still on disk or in the index, so a staged deletion no longer stops git add, and a rename counts as both of its names, so the old name's deletion is committed with the new one. A save that fails in the pulse hook is told to the agent. Tests: test_a_save_takes_deleted_and_renamed_files and test_a_save_that_fails_in_a_hook_is_told_to_the_agent (framework commit 2ebe661); both fail on the old code.

claim: A ticket file on the base branch with no branch and no ship is now recorded as `accepted by person via merge`, with no check that a person merged a contract pull request. Ticket files are excluded from the scope check, so an auto-merged LOW ticket whose branch adds `.rail/tickets/99.md` (tier HIGH, scope `.rail/engine/**`) gets the HIGH contract approved and claimed by the next `rail next` with no person involved; the engine on main showed the same ticket as `dropped`.
check: A test: commit a HIGH ticket file to the base branch under another ticket's `Ticket:` trailer, with no branch and no pull request, run `rail next`, and assert no `accepted` event with `by: person` is written.

claim: `_gh_named` treats any `gh` argument containing `github.com/` as naming a repository, including the value of `--body` or `-f`, so a merge of this project's pull request passes when its message mentions another repository's URL: `gh pr merge 5 --body "see github.com/other/repo"`. The engine on main denied this command; with the new rule that a merged unshipped pull request counts as the person's approval, it also lets an agent approve its own contract.
check: A guard test: `gh pr merge 5 --body "see github.com/other/repo"` and `gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/5/merge -f commit_message=https://github.com/other/repo/issues/1` must both return deny.

claim: The new Stop and PostToolUse hooks commit and push every untracked file inside `scope_paths` with no check, and `.gitignore` lists only `.claude/worktrees/` and `__pycache__/`. A credential or dump file an agent writes into an in-scope folder (for example `calc/token.json` under scope `calc/**`) is pushed to GitHub at the end of the turn, before verify's secret scan ever runs.
check: A test that `save_work` leaves out untracked files matching the guard's secret patterns (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`), or runs the project's secret scan before the push.

claim: The merge deny matches only `gh pr merge` with the two words adjacent, and the guard doesn't read command substitutions or `case` arms, so `gh pr -R timur-makarov/throw-away-repo merge 5`, `echo $(git push origin HEAD:main)` in backticks or `$(...)`, `case x in x) git push -f origin x;; esac` and `cd /tmp && export GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git && git push origin main` all pass. These passed on main's engine too.
check: Guard tests for each of these lines expecting deny.

reason: A merged contract now counts as the approval only when the ticket's own pull request (from its NN- branch) was merged; a ticket file on the base branch with no such pull request reads as dropped, as on main's engine. And a ticket's branch may no longer carry another ticket's file: only its own ticket file is outside scope_paths, at ship, in CI and in a save. Tests: test_a_ticket_file_that_came_in_with_another_merge_is_nobodys_approval (the reviewer's check) and test_a_tickets_branch_carries_no_other_tickets_file, framework commit 688f9aa; both fail on the old code.

A github.com URL names a repository only as an argument of its own, never inside an option's value, and for gh api only the endpoint counts. Both of the reviewer's commands are denied again, and so are gh pr -R OWNER/NAME merge and a full api.github.com endpoint of this repository. Tests: the added cases in test_a_merge_is_judged_by_the_repository_it_names (framework commit 688f9aa); they fail on the old guard.

A save leaves out files whose names say they hold secrets (.env files, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, *.keystore, SSH keys, .netrc) and tells the agent; they stay in the worktree for the ship, where verify runs first. Test: test_a_save_leaves_out_files_whose_names_say_they_hold_secrets (framework commit 688f9aa). A secret in a file with an innocent name is still pushed by a save: docs/loop.md says a save runs before verify.

claim: The PostToolUse throttle looks for its stamp under `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.git/rail/cache/pulse/`, but `rail hook pulse` writes it to the git common directory. In a session whose project directory is a git worktree (`.git` is a file there), the stamp is never found, so the pulse hook runs a fetch and a save after every tool call instead of at most every ten minutes, and commits and pushes in-scope changes each time.
check: A test that runs the PostToolUse command from settings.json twice with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set to a linked worktree and asserts the second call is skipped.

claim: The guard reads `GH_REPO` only as a prefix on the `gh` command itself, not when it is exported earlier in the line. So `cd OTHER_REPO && export GH_REPO=timur-makarov/throw-away-repo && gh pr merge 5` merges this project's pull request and is allowed; the engine on main allows it too, so this change did not cause it (an exported `GIT_DIR` is now followed, `GH_REPO` is not).
check: A guard test case: after `cd OTHER &&`, `export GH_REPO=<this repo> && gh pr merge 5` must be denied.

reason: The stamp is now the session's own file in the home folder (~/.cache/rail/pulse/SESSION): rail hook pulse writes it there and the PostToolUse command in .claude/settings.json looks there, so the throttle holds from any project folder, a worktree included. Test: test_the_pulse_hook_waits_as_long_in_a_session_that_stands_in_a_worktree (the reviewer's check; framework commit 4d2d7d9); it fails on the old code. The parked F15 is fixed too: an exported GH_REPO is followed.

claim: `quiet_minutes` counts every journal event as the claiming session's sign of life, including the `continued` event another session writes when it records a person's `rail:go`. Sequence: run-1 claims a ticket and ends, the ticket waits for a person (HOLD, RETRY_CAP, STUCK_REVIEW, an amend), the person adds `rail:go`, and the run that the label triggers records it and then reports the ticket as another session's work, quiet 0 min, with NO_WORK; the ticket is not resumed until a later run at least 30 minutes on, although docs/cloud.md says the label event covers `rail:go`.
check: A test on the fake GitHub: session run-1 claims a ticket with its events 45 minutes old, a person labels the pull request `rail:needs-you` and then `rail:go`, and `rail next` from session run-2 must answer with owner `agent` for that ticket, not NO_WORK with the ticket in `held`.

reason: The run that reads a person's rail:go on a ticket that waited for a person now takes the ticket over at once (the claiming session rested at the wait), and so does a session the person tells accept NN. A person's answer no longer counts as a sign of life of the claiming session either. Tests: test_the_run_that_reads_a_persons_go_takes_the_waiting_ticket_on (the reviewer's check, with a fresh claim, which is the harder case), test_an_answer_given_in_another_session_lets_that_session_go_on and test_a_go_on_a_ticket_at_work_leaves_the_claim_alone, framework commit 82ea206; all three fail on the old code.

claim: The new line scanner `_scan` doesn't know shell comments, so an apostrophe in a trailing comment opens a quote that swallows every following line: `echo start # can't fail` + newline + `git push origin HEAD:main` (or `gh api -X PUT repos/timur-makarov/throw-away-repo/pulls/5/merge`, or `git push -f`) passes the guard, though bash runs the second line. Main's engine denies these; a comment naming `<<EOF` or `$((1<<EOF))` hides the following lines the same way. With the new rule that a merged unshipped pull request is the person's approval, this also lets an agent approve its own contract.
check:
A guard test: for each denied command C, the two-line command `echo x # can't fail
C` is denied too, and so is `echo $((1<<EOF))
C
EOF`.

claim: `_gh_named` reads `GH_REPO=` from every word of the command, not only from the assignments in front of `gh`, so an option's value names a repository: `gh pr merge 5 --squash -t GH_REPO=other/repo` (or `--body GH_REPO=other/repo`) merges this project's pull request and passes. Main's engine denies it; this is F11's case with `GH_REPO=` in place of a URL.
check: A guard test: `gh pr merge 5 -t GH_REPO=other/repo` and `gh pr merge 5 --body GH_REPO=other/repo` are denied; only words before the command word count as assignments (raw[:len(raw)-len(words)]).

claim: The new tracking of an exported `GH_REPO` only ever adds: it counts an `export` that never reaches `gh` (in a pipeline, inside `bash -c`, a `declare` without `-x`) and ignores `unset GH_REPO`. So `export GH_REPO=other/repo; unset GH_REPO; gh pr merge 5` and `declare GH_REPO=other/repo; gh pr merge 5` merge this project's pull request and pass; main's engine denies all four.
check: A guard test: after `unset GH_REPO`, after an export inside a pipeline or `bash -c`, and after a `declare` without `-x`, `gh pr merge 5` is denied.

reason: The line reader now takes shell comments out, knows $'...' quoting and process substitution, and starts no here-document on a row that opened arithmetic; the tokenizer no longer treats a # inside a word as a comment. The reviewer's check is in test_the_guard_reads_command_lines_as_the_shell_does, and test_a_denied_command_is_found_wherever_the_shell_runs_it runs each denied command through 62 places a shell line can put a command (framework commit ee2129e); they fail on the old guard.

GH_REPO= names a repository only as an assignment in front of the gh command (raw[:len(raw)-len(words)]); in an option's value it names nothing. Test: the reviewer's two commands in test_a_merge_is_judged_by_the_repository_it_names (framework commit ee2129e).

An exported GH_REPO (and GIT_DIR) now only ever makes the guard stricter: it is believed when it names this project, never when it names another repository, so an export that doesn't reach gh (unset, a pipeline, a child shell, declare without -x) can't make a merge here pass. The reviewer's four commands are denied in test_a_merge_is_judged_by_the_repository_it_names (framework commit ee2129e). The parked F18 is fixed too: a cd after || or in a pipeline is not followed.

claim: `save_work` hands `git commit -- <paths>` names that git no longer knows or that `dirty` parsed wrongly. A file added to the index and then deleted from disk (`git add src/new.py; rm src/new.py`) makes one save exit 2 (the next passes), and an in-scope file whose name holds a double quote or ` -> ` makes every `rail save` and save hook fail, so no `saved` event is pushed and the ticket looks abandoned after 30 minutes.
check: A save test with (a) a file staged then removed from disk and (b) an untracked file named `src/q"x.py`, asserting `rail save` exits 0 and writes a `saved` event; reading names with `git status --porcelain -z` would make it pass.

reason: Real, and rare: it needs a file name with a double quote or an arrow in it, or a file staged and then deleted, and the reviewer rates it safe to merge. It is fixed in the framework (commit 110afb8: names are read with git status -z, and a save commits only what it records, with the reviewer's test). claim: A save with no file changes still pushes a `saved` event as a `[skip ci]` commit when the ticket has been quiet for `save_minutes`. Sequence: a ticket ships, its `rail` check fails more than ten minutes later (state `implementing`, RED_CHECK), and the Stop or pulse hook fires before the agent changes a file: the pull request's head becomes the `[skip ci]` commit, which has no check run and never gets one, so every later `rail next` in any session answers CI_WAIT with owner none, the red check is forgotten, and the ticket is neither resumed nor shown to a person.
check: A test: ship a ticket, mark its check failed on the fake GitHub, run `rail hook stop` with the clock past `save_minutes`, and assert `rail next` still answers RED_CHECK (or that the pull request's head did not move).

reason: A save with no changed file now writes nothing once the work has shipped, so the commit the ship pushed stays the pull request's head and its check keeps counting. Test: test_a_save_with_nothing_to_save_leaves_a_shipped_tickets_head_alone (the reviewer's check: the head doesn't move and rail next still answers RED_CHECK in both clones; framework commit cb18e10); it fails on the old code.

claim: After a ticket has shipped, a save with no in-scope file changed writes nothing, so a live session shows no sign of life until its first edit. Sequence: ticket ships, its check goes red (RED_CHECK, same for a blocking review finding), the claiming session investigates for 30 minutes with its pulse hook firing but no in-scope edit; another session's bare `rail next` then takes the ticket over. docs/loop.md and the `claim.save_minutes` text say a working session shows it is alive at least every ten minutes.
check: A test with the clock moved: ship, red check, the claiming session's pulse hook at +11, +22 and +29 minutes with no file changed, then `rail next` from a second session at +31 must leave the claim with the first session (for example by keeping the sign of life somewhere that doesn't move the pull request's head).

claim: While the agent is in the middle of the `git rebase main` that the failed ship's brief tells it to run, the worktree's HEAD is detached, so the engine doesn't see the worktree: a bare `rail next` picks RESUME and dies on `git worktree add ... already exists`. Main's engine has the same RESUME condition (`not f.worktree`), so this change did not cause it; the new save hooks skip the ticket silently in that state and leave the conflict untouched.
check: A test that stops a ticket's worktree in a conflicted rebase and runs `rail next`: it must answer in the usual shape, not exit with a git error.

reason: By design: a claim protects work in flight, and a shipped ticket that came back has none until a file changes. The other choice, a sign of life as a commit on the branch, is what F27 was: its [skip ci] commit hid the red check. A takeover in that window loses no work, and the first session is told to stand down at its next hook. The docs and the seed config said more than that (a sign of life at least every ten minutes); they now say it exactly, in the framework (commit b20f6cf), and this copy takes the wording with the next engine update.

reason: A gh pr merge is another repository's only in exact shapes: -R or --repo with OWNER/NAME, or the pull request as https://github.com/OWNER/NAME/pull/N, spelled with plain characters, with every other word a known option and at most one argument. A percent sign, a variable or any other address makes the command this project's wherever it runs; a scheme-less github.com/o/x is a branch name and proves nothing. The reviewer's lines are in test_a_merge_is_judged_by_the_repository_it_names (framework commit 1f31ac2), with most of the parked F46: -R taken as another option's value, a merge path by repository id from another folder, and the cloud's auto_merge path.

claim: The new machine-level guard steps aside for a project whenever the file `rail/cache/hooks/<session id>` exists in that repository's git directory, and that file is writable by any command the agent runs. In a session above several repositories, where the machine hooks are the only guard, `mkdir -p repo/.git/rail/cache/hooks && echo 1 > repo/.git/rail/cache/hooks/$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` makes `cd repo && git push -f origin x` (and pushes to main, and merges) pass with no judgement for the rest of the session.
check: A test that writes the marker by hand in a session whose repository hooks did not run, then expects `rail hook guard --machine` to still deny `cd repo && git push -f origin x`; or have the guard deny Bash writes into `rail/cache/hooks`.

claim: Several forms still run a denied command in this project and pass, on main's engine too: a `cd` the shell doesn't perform as the guard reads it (`cd () (true)` or `shopt -s expand_aliases; alias cd=true` on an earlier line, `2>/dev/null cd <repo> && ...`, `trap 'cd <repo>' DEBUG`), a command in a `trap ... EXIT`, a flag after an argument that spans lines (`git push origin x "<newline>" --force`), and from another repository `git -c remote.origin.url=<this repo> push -f origin x` or `git push -f --repo=<this repo>`.

The `--owner` ask is still dodged when `rail` isn't the command's first word or the flag isn't literal: `python3 .rail/bin/rail answer 5 F1 declined why --owner` passes with no ask, and so would `O=--owner; rail answer 5 F1 declined why $O`. Main's engine and the permission rules don't catch these either. Likewise nothing stops an agent adding the `rail:go` label itself through `gh api .../issues/N/labels`, which the engine reads as the person's approval.

Pull requests are keyed by head branch name alone, with no check that the head is in this repository, so on a public repository a fork's pull request from a branch named like an open ticket's (`10-slug`) becomes that ticket's pull request once it is the newest. Closing it makes the ticket read as dropped, and its comments reach the agent as the person's note. The same line is on main; read from the code, not run.
check: A forge test where the newest pull request for a ticket's branch name has `head.repo.full_name` different from the project's repository, expecting it to be ignored.

reason: Real, and it takes a deliberate act: the agent has to write a marker file into a repository's .git folder to make the machine-level guard step aside. The guard is there to stop mistakes and says so (docs/guards.md: guards prevent mistakes, they are not a boundary; a script file is not read either); what holds against an agent that wants around it is the ruleset on GitHub. Hardening it, by denying shell writes under rail/cache as for the journal, goes into the framework as its own change and comes with the next engine update, so this change is not reviewed a thirty-second time for it.
